nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: General linear model (GLM) was used to construct a normative brain volume model from healthy controls. The model estimated the relationship between brain volume and covariates (age, sex, TIV). Individual structural abnormality maps (SAM) were generated by calculating W-scores, which quantify the deviation of each patient's voxel-wise brain volume from the normative model.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM) volumes were extracted from T1 images using CAT12. The normalized GM and WM images were smoothed with a 4-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel. Separate normative models were constructed for GM and WM volumes.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: the whole brain image was segmented into different tissue types, e.g., gray matter (GM), white matter (WM) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), followed by normalization of the segmented GM and WM images into the MNI space

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model included three explanatory variables: age, sex, and total intracranial volume (TIV). These were used as regressors in the GLM to model the expected brain volume for each voxel.
